assessment: This paper provides an alternative theory about taste coding in larval insects. The authors use a volumetric imaging method to capture neural activity from an entire taste sensory organ in Drosophila larvae. Their results suggest that taste coding in Drosophila larvae might be different than adult flies, and use multimodal neurons and neural dynamics to represent taste information in the larval brain. Understanding taste coding in Drosophila larvae might provide further understanding to how food is encoded in the larval insect brain.
